item.title: Middle East live: Trump says he won’t 'be much more patient’ with Iran
item.description: US President Donald Trump ​said he would not be ​much ‌more ⁠patient with ‌Iran as he urged Tehran ⁠to reach a deal ​with Washington. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments in the Middle East.

item.title: Why did Saudi Arabia and the UAE allegedly carry out secret bombing raids on Iran?
item.description: The United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia in April secretly carried out a series of air strikes against Iran during the US-Israeli war against Tehran, the Wall Street Journal and Reuters reported this week. Analysts say these raids – which neither country has confirmed – would have been clandestine counterattacks following Tehran’s drone and missile strikes against Gulf state infrastructure.

item.title: Lebanese split over diplomatic normalisation amid Washington talks
item.description: In Lebanon, the very idea of peace with Israel continues to deeply divide opinion. As unprecedented negotiations open today in Washington under US mediation, many Lebanese see a chance for a return to stability. But within Hezbollah’s camp, any normalization with Israel is firmly rejected. Report by Serge Berberi and Renee Davis.

item.title: Abu Dhabi 'doesn't want to appear too much in cooperation with Israel', analyst says
item.description: A renewed escalation in the Strait of Hormuz saw the seizure on Thursday of a ship anchored off the Unites Arab Emirates coast. Earlier Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had announced he had quietly visited the UAE during the Israeli-U.S. war with Iran, though the UAE swiftly denied that any secret visit had occurred. item.title: Iran accuses United Arab Emirates of being 'active partner' in US-Israeli war
item.description: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi accused the United Arab Emirates on Thursday of playing an active role in the US-Israeli war against his country. Araghchi also referred to what Israel has described as a "secret" meeting in the UAE during the war between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Emirati President Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan -- a visit Abu Dhabi denied took place. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

item.title: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire nears end: Will fresh talks lead to new truce?
item.description: Israel's ruling coalition on Wednesday submitted a proposal to dissolve parliament to pave the way for early elections. The move, initiated by Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party, came as Netanyahu appeared to be facing a possible collapse of his fractious coalition, amid mounting pressure from the ultra-Orthodox parties. item.title: Israel launches fresh strikes on Lebanon despite ceasefire and ongoing talks
item.description: The conflict between Israel and Hezbollah is continuing despite talks currently taking place between Lebanon and Israel. On Wednesday, twelve people were killed by Israeli strikes on Lebanon, according to the country's health ministry. Story by James Vasina.

item.title: Trump says Xi offered help to open Hormuz, vowed not to arm Iran
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Thursday said President Xi Jinping had offered China's help to open the Strait of Hormuz and pledged not to send military equipment to aid Iran in its war against the US and Israel.

item.title: Israel, Lebanon hold 'positive' Washington talks as US seeks ceasefire extension
item.description: The United States on Thursday pushed to extend a fragile Israel-Lebanon ceasefire ahead of its Sunday expiry, as President Donald Trump voiced optimism over China’s efforts on Iran. Violence flared as Israeli and Lebanese officials met in Washington, while Israeli strikes in Lebanon continued despite the truce remaining formally in place.
